extracted.intended_audience: users of PARI/GP (mathematicians, computational number theorists, and programmers using PARI for number-theoretic computations)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library routines (Dirichlet characters, factoring, continued fractions, finite-field tools, etc.), giving input types, behavior, return formats, examples, and warnings. Useful for writing and debugging scripts that use these number-theory functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conrey vs SNF character representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Dirichlet characters on (Z/NZ)* may be represented as t_INT (Conrey label), t_COL (Conrey logarithm in terms of Conrey generators), or t_VEC (in terms of SNF generators). The t_COL (Conrey logarithms) format is the preferred/fastest representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains Conrey generators (Chinese remainders, lifted generators per prime power), Conrey logarithm (column vector of discrete logs w.r.t. Conrey generators), and attached Conrey character. Notes that Conrey generators need not satisfy SNF; any m in (Z/NZ)* decomposes uniquely as product of Conrey generators to exponents modulo Di. Use znconreychar, znconreylog, znconreyexp to convert between formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: addprimes: manage user-defined extra primes
rubrics_metrics.description: addprimes(x = []) adds integers in vector x (or single integer x) to a table of user-defined primes which future factor calls will trial divide by; returns that table. If x omitted or empty, returns current list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must be primes (no internal primality check). To remove use removeprimes. Library syntax: GEN addprimes(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: bestappr: best rational approximation / modular reconstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: bestappr(x, {B}) returns a rational approximation a/b to x with denominator ≤ B. For t_REAL/t_FRAC uses continued fractions; for t_INTMOD or t_PADIC performs rational modular reconstruction modulo N, returning unique a/b with |a| < N/2B and b ≤ B congruent to x modulo N. If B omitted choose best possible; if reconstruction impossible returns [].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B must be positive real when provided (0 < b ≤ B). Omitting B for modular case chooses B of order N/2. Applies recursively to components of complex objects; if any entry fails, returns []. Examples: bestappr(Pi,100)=355/113, bestappr(Mod(...)) can return [] if no reconstruction. Library syntax: GEN bestappr(GEN x, GEN B = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: bestapprPade: best rational-function (Padé) approximation
rubrics_metrics.description: bestapprPade(x, {B}) returns a rational function a/b approximating x with degree(b) ≤ B (if B omitted, choose best available). For t_POLMOD modulo N performs rational modular reconstruction of rational function; for t_RFRAC or t_SER implicitly converts to t_POLMOD. If no suitable a/b exists returns [].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B must be non-negative (0 ≤ degree(b) ≤ B). Omitting B chooses floor(degree(N)/2) for modular case. Applies recursively to components; if any entry fails, returns []. Library syntax: GEN bestapprPade(GEN x, long B).

rubrics_metrics.name: bezout / gcdext alias
rubrics_metrics.description: bezout(x,y) is a deprecated alias for gcdext; use gcdext0(GEN x, GEN y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax provided for backward compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: bigomega: count prime factors with multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: bigomega(x) returns the number of prime divisors of integer |x| counted with multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: factor(392) shows factorization, bigomega(392)=5, while omega(392)=2 (without multiplicity). Library syntax: long bigomega(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: binomial: binomial coefficient for non-integer x
rubrics_metrics.description: binomial(x,y) computes binomial coefficient; y must be integer but x can be any PARI object representing a scalar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN binomial(GEN x, long y). Variants and helper functions like vecbinome available.

rubrics_metrics.name: charconj: conjugate of a character
rubrics_metrics.description: charconj(cyc, chi) returns the conjugate character for a finite abelian group represented by its elementary divisors cyc and character vector chi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: cyc can be any object with .cyc method (e.g., znstar or bnrinit). For Dirichlet characters (idealstar), Conrey representations are available. Examples provided. Library syntax: GEN charconj0(GEN cyc, GEN chi) and faster unchecked variant GEN charconj.

rubrics_metrics.name: chardiv: divide two characters
rubrics_metrics.description: chardiv(cyc, a, b) returns the quotient character a/b (componentwise product with inverse) for characters on an abelian group represented by cyc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inputs are in same format, result is in same format; otherwise a Conrey logarithm is used. For Dirichlet characters additional Conrey formats available. Examples and library syntax given; unchecked variant exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: chareval: evaluate a character at an element
rubrics_metrics.description: chareval(G, chi, x, {z}) returns the value of character chi on element x of abelian group G supporting discrete log methods (e.g., idealstar for (Z/qZ)* or bnr structures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional z controls output encoding: omitted => rational c(x)/o with 0 ≤ c(x) < o or -1 sentinel when x not in group; z integer o => return integer c(x) or -1 sentinel; z = [zeta,o] => return ζ^{c(x)} or 0 sentinel; z = [vzeta,o] => table lookup via vector of powers. Note on general character encoding and Dirichlet-specific formats. Library syntax: GEN chareval(GEN G, GEN chi, GEN x, GEN z).

rubrics_metrics.name: charker: compute kernel subgroup of a character
rubrics_metrics.description: charker(cyc, chi) returns the kernel of character chi as an HNF matrix K whose columns give generators of the subgroup; determinant of K is the kernel index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: cyc may be any object with .cyc method. For Dirichlet characters Conrey representation interplay noted. Library syntax: GEN charker0(GEN cyc, GEN chi) and unchecked variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: charmul: multiply two characters
rubrics_metrics.description: charmul(cyc, a, b) returns the product character ab for characters on group cyc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both characters are in same format, result is in that format; otherwise a Conrey logarithm is used. Examples for Dirichlet characters and library syntax provided, plus unchecked variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: charorder: order of a character
rubrics_metrics.description: charorder(cyc, chi) returns the multiplicative order of the character chi on the abelian group represented by cyc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works for general groups with .cyc method and for Dirichlet characters (Conrey formats available). Examples and library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: chinese: Chinese remainder combination
rubrics_metrics.description: chinese(x, {y}) constructs a representative z congruent to x modulo first modulus and to y modulo second modulus, when x and y are intmods or polmods; supports vector/matrix by recursive application; if y omitted and x vector returns residue class common to components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For polynomial arguments in same variable, applied to each coefficient; warns about high-degree copying behavior and suggests converting polynomials to equal-length vectors first. chinese(x,x) = x. Library syntax: GEN chinese(GEN x, GEN y = NULL) and GEN chinese1(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: content: gcd of coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: content(x) computes the gcd of all coefficients of x when that makes sense (polynomial, power series, vector/matrix). For scalar rational returns absolute value; for inexact inputs returns 1 or x depending on exactness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content of rational function is ratio of numerator and denominator contents. Recursive structures treat matrix/vector coefficient by computing their content. t_VECSMALL entries assumed signed integers. Library syntax: GEN content(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: contfrac: continued fraction partial quotients
rubrics_metrics.description: contfrac(x, {b}, {nmax}) returns row vector of partial quotients of continued fraction expansion of x; if b supplied uses generalized continued fraction with numerators b; nmax limits number of partial quotients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalized so last partial quotient an = 1 (unless n=0). If nmax omitted stops at last significant quotient. For numerical x ai are integers; for rational functions ai are polynomials. If vector b provided length equals #b unless unreliable. Obsolete hack: contfrac(x,,b) may interpret b as nmax. Examples and implementation note given. Library syntax: GEN contfrac0(GEN x, GEN b = NULL, long nmax).

rubrics_metrics.name: contfracpnqn: convergents from continued fraction data
rubrics_metrics.description: contfracpnqn(x, {n=-1}) given partial quotients vector returns 2x2 matrix [pn, pn-1; qn, qn-1] so pn/qn equals the continued fraction convergent; if n≥0 returns all convergents up to pn/qn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows generalized continued fractions when x is two-row matrix [b_row; a_row]. Library syntax: GEN contfracpnqn(GEN x, long n) (also pnqn for n=-1). Examples given computing convergents of Pi expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: core: squarefree part of integer
rubrics_metrics.description: core(n, {flag=0}) returns d where n = d f^2 with d squarefree; if flag non-zero returns [d,f]. By convention core(0,1) returns [0,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN core0(GEN n, long flag). Also GEN core(GEN n) and GEN core2(GEN n) for flag variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: coredisc: fundamental discriminant extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: coredisc(n, {flag=0}) returns unique fundamental discriminant d with n = d f^2 and f positive rational; if flag non-zero returns [d,f]. coredisc(0,1) returns [0,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes on congruence conditions for fundamental discriminants, relation to quaddisc, and integer/half-integer f depending on n mod 4. Library syntax variants: GEN coredisc0, coredisc, coredisc2.

rubrics_metrics.name: dirdiv: divide Dirichlet series represented as vectors
rubrics_metrics.description: dirdiv(x,y) with x,y vectors (possibly different lengths) representing Dirichlet series computes quotient x/y as a vector, assuming y[1] ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN dirdiv(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: direuler: compute Dirichlet series from Euler product
rubrics_metrics.description: direuler(p = a, b, expr, {c}) computes Dirichlet series attached to Euler product ∏_{p=a..b} expr(p^{-s}) and returns vector of coefficients; if c omitted returns first b coefficients else first c coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting c < b is useless; if c > b computed coefficients include missing Euler factors (zeros) for primes beyond range. expr must be polynomial/rational in auxiliary variable X. Library syntax details provided (low-level interface). Examples compute sigma function series.

rubrics_metrics.name: dirmul: multiply Dirichlet series represented as vectors
rubrics_metrics.description: dirmul(x,y) computes product of Dirichlet-series-vectors x and y (possibly different lengths) giving vector of coefficients of product; product length = min(#x * v(y), #y * v(x)) where v(x) is index of first non-zero coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show behavior with sequences including leading zeros. Library syntax: GEN dirmul(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: divisors: list divisors of an object
rubrics_metrics.description: divisors(x) returns row vector of divisors of x; for integer returns positive divisors in increasing order; for general objects divisors are products of irreducible factors to nonnegative powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factorization via factor(n) can be used to generate divisors. Library syntax: GEN divisors(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: eulerphi: Euler's totient function conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: eulerphi(x) returns φ(|x|) cardinality of (Z/xZ)^*. By convention φ(0) := 2 (Z* = {−1,1}), consistent with znstar(0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN eulerphi(GEN x). Example eulerphi(40)=16.

rubrics_metrics.name: factor: general factoring across domains and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: factor(x, {lim}) factors integers, rationals, Gaussian integers, rational functions and polynomials across supported domains (Q, R, C, Qp, finite fields, number fields), returning two-column matrix [irreducible, exponent]. For integers returns pseudoprimes by default (<=2^64 genuine primes). lim (t_INT) can limit search to primes p < lim (deprecated semantics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: 0 factored as 0^1; factoring uses trial division, perfect power tests, different algorithms (factorint is specialized for integer factoring), factor may produce pseudoprimes for large factors; set global factor_proven or use isprime to prove primality. For polynomials, content discarded; use content() if needed. Gives guidance on choosing domain-specific factor functions (factormod, factorff, factorpadic, nffactor) and warnings about inexact coefficients implying assumed squarefree inputs. Library syntax: GEN gp_factor0, and recommended GEN factor(GEN x) or GEN boundfact. Many examples, performance notes, and warnings about relying on global variables or deprecated lim=0. Mentions factorint and factorint alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorback: reconstruct object from factorization
rubrics_metrics.description: factorback(f, {e}) reconstructs original object from factorization f (and optional exponents e); integer 1 corresponds to empty factorization. If e omitted and f is vector treated as factors with exponent 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples for integer 12, vectors, and normal factorization formats. Library syntax: GEN factorback2(GEN f, GEN e = NULL) or GEN factorback(GEN f).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorcantor: factor polynomials mod p using Cantor–Zassenhaus
rubrics_metrics.description: factorcantor(x, p) factors polynomial x modulo prime p using distinct-degree + Cantor–Zassenhaus; coefficients must be compatible with Z/pZ. Returns two-column matrix [irreducible polynomials, exponents]. factormod usually faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only irreducible degrees needed use factormod(...,flag=1). Library syntax: GEN factcantor(GEN x, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorff: factor polynomials over finite field F_q
rubrics_metrics.description: factorff(x, {p}, {a}) factors polynomial x in field F_q defined by irreducible polynomial a over F_p; returns two-column matrix [factors, exponents]. If all coefficients are in F_p a faster algorithm used. If x has t_FFELT coefficients a or p may be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative syntaxes: pass q = p^f or pair [p,f] or provide defining polynomial P to infer p. If insufficient info, error; examples show typical usage and more readable syntax when coefficients are t_FFELT. Library syntax: GEN factorff(GEN x, GEN p = NULL, GEN a = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorial / mpfact / mpfactr distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: factorial(x) returns real approximation of x! while operator x! returns integer, mpfact and mpfactr variants return integer t_INT or real with precision respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mpfact(long x) returns x! as t_INT; GEN mpfactr(long x, long prec) for real result with precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorint: integer factoring engine and flags
rubrics_metrics.description: factorint(x, {flag=0}) factors integer n into pseudoprimes using SQUFOF, Pollard Rho, ECM, MPQS, and pure power search; returns two-column matrix of 'prime' divisors and exponents. By default large factors > 2^64 are pseudoprimes (BPSW tested); use isprime or set factor_proven to 1 to prove primality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag bits: 1 avoid MPQS, 2 skip first-stage ECM, 4 avoid Rho/SQUFOF, 8 skip final ECM (may declare huge composite prime). Debugging via gp's debug default parameter. This is the integer factoring backend used by many functions. Library syntax: GEN factorint(GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: factormod: factor polynomial modulo prime via Berlekamp
rubrics_metrics.description: factormod(x, p, {flag=0}) factors polynomial x modulo prime p using Berlekamp; returns two-column matrix [irreducible factors, exponents]; if flag non-zero outputs only degrees of irreducibles. factormod is usually faster than factorcantor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coefficients must be operation-compatible with Z/pZ. Library syntax: GEN factormod0(GEN x, GEN p, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffgen: finite-field element generator
rubrics_metrics.description: ffgen(q, {v}) returns a t_FFELT generator for finite field with q elements (q = p^f). It computes an irreducible monic polynomial P ∈ F_p[X] of degree f and returns g = X mod P. If v provided use variable name display; alternative syntaxes accept pair [p,f] or directly input polynomial P (monic irreducible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If q not a prime power error; if P provided must be irreducible or resulting t_FFELT may be invalid (irreducibility test more costly than generating via ffinit). Library syntax: GEN ffgen(GEN q, long v = -1). Helper to create generator for prime field provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: ffinit: compute irreducible polynomial over Fp
rubrics_metrics.description: ffinit(p, n, {v = 'x'}) computes a monic irreducible polynomial of degree n over F_p using fast variant of Adleman–Lenstra algorithm; useful for ffgen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ffinit(GEN p, long n, long v = -1). Example usage with ffgen described.

rubrics_metrics.name: fflog: discrete logarithm in finite field
rubrics_metrics.description: fflog(x, g, {o}) computes discrete logarithm e such that g^e = x in finite field; if o provided it is multiplicative order of g (preferred format [ord, factor(ord)]). If o omitted assume g primitive. Result undefined if e doesn't exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm choices: generic discrete log and cubic-sieve index calculus for large fields of degree≥5; Coppersmith for small characteristic fields (≤5). Examples and library syntax: GEN fflog(GEN x, GEN g, GEN o = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffnbirred: count irreducible polynomials over finite field
rubrics_metrics.description: ffnbirred(q, n, {fl=0}) computes number of monic irreducible polynomials over F_q of degree exactly n (flag=0) or at most n (flag=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ffnbirred0(GEN q, long n, long fl); convenience wrappers ffnbirred and ffsumnbirred exist.
